Corrections and release history

Material corrections to published evidence and superseded records, and how they are recorded.

Start with a questionVerify evidence
Understand → Explore → Verify

This resource presents the strongest defensible answer while keeping scope, limits and source visible.

01

What is recorded

Material changes are recorded: changes to a public value, definition, supporting evidence, source link, derivation, reuse conditions or interpretation. Wording or layout edits that do not change meaning are not listed as corrections.

02

How history works

Material corrections are recorded against stable evidence IDs and release information so earlier citations can still be understood. Where a prior version can be retained publicly and safely, it remains identifiable; where it cannot, the correction note records enough information to explain the change.

03

No silent material correction

A material correction updates the published result, its evidence record and this correction log at the same time.

04

Cite the active record and release

After a correction, cite the active record and release unless you are intentionally citing a historical version. The current record should retain a visible correction note whenever a material earlier state affected public interpretation.

Current record and correction path

This resource does not manufacture a release or correction history. A correction event appears only when it is governed for publication; the stable record ID remains the route back to the current public record.

This page currently has no separately governed material-correction events to publish, so the interface does not invent a synthetic history.
